facts.statement: The International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 is Act No. 50 of 2019 and received assent on 19 December 2019.
facts.detail: Short title: International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019.

facts.statement: The IFSCA Act commenced in three stages: Sections 1-11, 14-16, 27, 29, 30, 34 on 27 April 2020; Sections 12, 17-26, 28, 31, 32 on 21 August 2020; Sections 13 and 33 on 1 October 2020.
facts.detail: IFSCA was established 27 April 2020 and assumed the powers of RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA for IFSCs on 1 October 2020.

facts.statement: The IFSCA Act applies only to International Financial Services Centres set up under Section 18 of the SEZ Act, 2005, whether before or after the IFSCA Act's commencement.
facts.detail: Only one IFSC is permitted per SEZ.
facts.source_ref: application clause; S.18 SEZ Act link

facts.statement: Under Section 3(d), 'financial product' means securities, contracts of insurance, deposits, credit arrangements, and foreign currency contracts excluding contracts for immediate settlement, plus any notified product.
facts.detail: Foreign exchange spot (immediate settlement) contracts are excluded from the definition.

facts.statement: Section 3(e) defines 'financial service' through 14 sub-clauses including accepting deposits, safeguarding assets, effecting contracts of insurance, managing assets, operating investment schemes, maintaining ownership records, underwriting, providing credit information, issuing stored-value or payment instruments, arranging services, and advising or soliciting.

The IFSCA Authority consists of 9 members: a Chairperson, 4 ex officio members nominated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA, 2 Ministry of Finance officials, and 2 members appointed on the Selection Committee's recommendation.
facts.detail: The Chairperson is whole-time; members under S.5(1)(d) may be whole-time or part-time.

facts.statement: The Chairperson and members of IFSCA hold office for 3 years and are eligible for re-appointment; maximum age is 65 years for the Chairperson and 62 years for whole-time members.
facts.detail: Resignation requires 3 months' notice. Post-service cooling-off: 2 years during which no Central/State government employment or appointment by an IFSC financial institution is permitted without prior Central Government approval.

facts.statement: Grounds for removing the Chairperson or a member under Section 7: insolvency, physical or mental incapacity, conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude, prejudicial financial interest, and abuse of position; the last two grounds require a hearing opportunity.
IFSCA decisions are by majority vote with a casting vote for the Chairperson, and a member with a conflict of interest must recuse from the relevant deliberation.

The Performance Review Committee under Section 17 has at least 2 members, reviews IFSCA's performance at least once per financial year, and submits its report to the Central Government within 3 months of receipt.
IFSCA must submit its annual report to the Central Government within 90 days after the end of each financial year.
The Central Government may supersede IFSCA for a maximum period of 6 months under Section 22.
Transactions of the Authority under Section 20 must be in specified foreign currency.
Under Section 26 the IFSCA Authority is exempt from income-tax and all other taxes.
Section 30 gives the IFSCA Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws, and the power to remove difficulties under Section 32 expires 5 years after commencement.

The First Schedule transfers powers over IFSCs across 14 Acts from 4 regulators: RBI (7 Acts: RBI Act 1934, Banking Regulation Act 1949, DICGC Act 1961, FEMA 1999, Credit Information Companies Act 2005, Government Securities Act 2006, Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007), SEBI (3: SCRA 1956, SEBI Act 1992, Depositories Act 1996), IRDAI (3: Insurance Act 1938, GIC Nationalisation Act 1972, IRDAI Act 1999), and PFRDA (1: PFRDA Act 2013).
facts.detail: IFSCA assumed these powers on 1 October 2020. The Second Schedule amends the same 14 enactments to insert 'powers not to apply to IFSC' provisions.

facts.statement: Penalties and fines collected by IFSCA under Section 13(5) are collected in the foreign-currency equivalent and credited to the Consolidated Fund of India in Indian rupees.

IFSCA's mandate covers development as well as regulation, supervision and enforcement for financial products, financial services and financial institutions in IFSCs; functions are under Section 12 and powers under Section 13.
facts.detail: IFSCA is a body corporate with perpetual succession headquartered at GIFT City (Section 4). The Fund of the Authority is under Section 15.

facts.statement: The IFSCA Chairperson as of 2025 is K. Rajaraman (IAS), who succeeded Injeti Srinivas.
